chunks: Then the opponent of occultation is asked, 'Is it possible that the occultation may have a valid reason that has caused it and a wise explanation that has prompted it or it is not possible?'

If he should say, 'It is possible,' he will be told, 'Then why does occultation lead you to conclude the non-existence of the Imam in this time despite considering it possible that it may have a reason not incompatible with the existence of Imam?'

Is it not like the argument of a person, who negates the wisdom of the Creator on the basis of pains and diseases of children, notwithstanding his acknowledgement that their pains and diseases may have a valid explanation that does not violate divine wisdom?'

Or the argument of a person who argues on the basis of the superficialities of 'ambiguous verses' that the Almighty is similar to physical bodies and creates the actions of people, despite his profession that these verses may have valid interpretations that do not violate the principles of wisdom, Divine justice, monotheism and negation of His physicality.'

key_terms.الْغَيْبَة: Occultation (the state of being hidden from public view)

ai.seo_question: What is the logical argument for the wisdom behind the Imam's occultation?
ai.summary: Al-Tusi employs a reductio ad absurdum argument, comparing the occultation to other accepted theological paradoxes such as the wisdom behind the suffering of children or the apparent anthropomorphism in ambiguous Quranic verses. He argues that just as opponents accept hidden wisdom in these cases without denying God's attributes, they must similarly accept the Imam's hidden presence despite the apparent delay, thereby refuting the claim that occultation proves absence.
